+import { isActive } from './entities';
+import { addDays, comparePlainDates, daysBetween } from './plainDate';
+import { timestampToMs } from './schedule';
+import { dueDate, overdueTasks, pendingOnDate } from './window';
+import { startOfDayMs } from './zone';
+import type { Id, Item, PlainDate, Timestamp } from './types';
+
+/*
+ * What the Timeline shows for one day. Analogy: each day is a page of a paper planner. The top of
+ * the page has a strip for what is open on your desk (tasks inside their window), then the items
+ * that happen that day: whole-day ones first, then the ones with a time, in time order. An item
+ * that spans several days is written on every page it touches, with a "continues" mark on the
+ * pages where it did not start or does not end.
+ *
+ * Days are cut in the display time zone, so a day can have 23 or 25 hours.
+ */
+
+export interface TimelineEntry {
+  item: Item;
+  /** Whole-day items have no hour. Timed ones are placed by hour. */
+  type: 'allDay' | 'timed';
+  /** The item started on an earlier day, so this page shows a "continues from" mark. */
+  continuesFromPrevious: boolean;
+  /** The item goes on after this day, so this page shows a "continues on" mark. */
+  continuesToNext: boolean;
+  /** Timed items only: the part of the item inside this day, as instants in milliseconds. */
+  startMs: number | null;
+  endMs: number | null;
+}
+
+export interface OpenTask {
+  item: Item;
+  /** The day of the delivery, to highlight it. */
+  dueDate: PlainDate;
+  isDueDay: boolean;
+}
+
+export interface TimelineDay {
+  date: PlainDate;
+  /** Whole-day events and work blocks. */
+  allDay: TimelineEntry[];
+  /** Timed events and work blocks, in time order. */
+  timed: TimelineEntry[];
+  /** Tasks pending on this day (inside their window, not done), the delivery day first. */
+  open: OpenTask[];
+  /** True when there is nothing at all, so the view can fold the day. */
+  empty: boolean;
+}
+
+export interface OverdueEntry {
+  item: Item;
+  dueDate: PlainDate;
+  /**
+   * Whole days between the delivery day and the reference day. Zero means the delivery was today
+   * and its time already passed (late today), so only timed deliveries can have a zero.
+   */
+  daysLate: number;
+}
+
+const byTitle = (a: Item, b: Item) =>
+  a.title.localeCompare(b.title) || (a.id < b.id ? -1 : a.id > b.id ? 1 : 0);
+
+/** Events that can sit on a day: not deleted, with a schedule. Tasks never use `schedule`. */
+function scheduledEvents(items: readonly Item[]): Item[] {
+  return items.filter((item) => isActive(item) && item.kind === 'event' && item.schedule !== null);
+}
+
+function entryForDay(
+  item: Item,
+  date: PlainDate,
+  dayStart: number,
+  dayEnd: number,
+): TimelineEntry | null {
+  const schedule = item.schedule!;
+
+  if (schedule.allDay) {
+    const last = schedule.end ?? schedule.start;
+    if (comparePlainDates(date, schedule.start) < 0 || comparePlainDates(date, last) > 0) {
+      return null;
+    }
+    return {
+      item,
+      type: 'allDay',
+      continuesFromPrevious: comparePlainDates(schedule.start, date) < 0,
+      continuesToNext: comparePlainDates(last, date) > 0,
+      startMs: null,
+      endMs: null,
+    };
+  }
+
+  const start = timestampToMs(schedule.start);
+  const end = schedule.end === undefined ? start : timestampToMs(schedule.end);
+  const isPoint = end <= start;
+
+  // An item with no length belongs to the day of its start. One with a length touches the day
+  // when it overlaps it. Ending exactly at midnight does not reach the next day.
+  const touches = isPoint ? start >= dayStart && start < dayEnd : start < dayEnd && end > dayStart;
+  if (!touches) return null;
+
+  return {
+    item,
+    type: 'timed',
+    continuesFromPrevious: start < dayStart,
+    continuesToNext: !isPoint && end > dayEnd,
+    startMs: Math.max(start, dayStart),
+    endMs: isPoint ? start : Math.min(end, dayEnd),
+  };
+}
+
+function buildDay(
+  events: readonly Item[],
+  allItems: readonly Item[],
+  date: PlainDate,
+  displayTimeZone: string,
+  doneIds: ReadonlySet<Id>,
+): TimelineDay {
+  const dayStart = startOfDayMs(date, displayTimeZone);
+  const dayEnd = startOfDayMs(addDays(date, 1), displayTimeZone);
+
+  const entries = events
+    .map((item) => entryForDay(item, date, dayStart, dayEnd))
+    .filter((entry): entry is TimelineEntry => entry !== null);
+
+  const allDay = entries
+    .filter((entry) => entry.type === 'allDay')
+    .sort(
+      (a, b) =>
+        comparePlainDates(
+          (a.item.schedule as { start: PlainDate }).start,
+          (b.item.schedule as { start: PlainDate }).start,
+        ) || byTitle(a.item, b.item),
+    );
+
+  const timed = entries
+    .filter((entry) => entry.type === 'timed')
+    .sort((a, b) => a.startMs! - b.startMs! || a.endMs! - b.endMs! || byTitle(a.item, b.item));
+
+  const open = pendingOnDate(allItems, date, displayTimeZone, doneIds)
+    .map((item) => {
+      const due = dueDate(item.due!, displayTimeZone);
+      return { item, dueDate: due, isDueDay: due === date };
+    })
+    .sort(
+      (a, b) =>
+        Number(b.isDueDay) - Number(a.isDueDay) ||
+        comparePlainDates(a.dueDate, b.dueDate) ||
+        byTitle(a.item, b.item),
+    );
+
+  return { date, allDay, timed, open, empty: entries.length === 0 && open.length === 0 };
+}
+
+/** One day of the Timeline. */
+export function buildTimelineDay(
+  items: readonly Item[],
+  date: PlainDate,
+  displayTimeZone: string,
+  doneIds: ReadonlySet<Id>,
+): TimelineDay {
+  return buildDay(scheduledEvents(items), items, date, displayTimeZone, doneIds);
+}
+
+/** Consecutive days from `from` to `to`, both included. Empty when `to` comes before `from`. */
+export function buildTimelineRange(
+  items: readonly Item[],
+  from: PlainDate,
+  to: PlainDate,
+  displayTimeZone: string,
+  doneIds: ReadonlySet<Id>,
+): TimelineDay[] {
+  const count = daysBetween(from, to) + 1;
+  if (count <= 0) return [];
+  const events = scheduledEvents(items);
+  return Array.from({ length: count }, (_, index) =>
+    buildDay(events, items, addDays(from, index), displayTimeZone, doneIds),
+  );
+}
+
+/**
+ * The overdue strip: tasks whose delivery has passed and that are not done, oldest delivery
+ * first, each with how many days late it is on the reference day (normally today).
+ */
+export function buildOverdueStrip(
+  items: readonly Item[],
+  now: Timestamp,
+  referenceDate: PlainDate,
+  displayTimeZone: string,
+  doneIds: ReadonlySet<Id>,
+): OverdueEntry[] {
+  return overdueTasks(items, now, displayTimeZone, doneIds).map((item) => {
+    const due = dueDate(item.due!, displayTimeZone);
+    return { item, dueDate: due, daysLate: Math.max(0, daysBetween(due, referenceDate)) };
+  });
+}

+import { isActive } from './entities';
+import type { Id, Item, SyncFields } from './types';
+
+type Node = SyncFields & { parentId: Id | null };
+
+/** The ids from the top of the tree down to the entity itself. Stops if the data has a cycle. */
+export function pathFromRoot<T extends Node>(id: Id, byId: ReadonlyMap<Id, T>): T[] {
+  const path: T[] = [];
+  const seen = new Set<Id>();
+  let current = byId.get(id);
+  while (current && !seen.has(current.id)) {
+    seen.add(current.id);
+    path.push(current);
+    current = current.parentId === null ? undefined : byId.get(current.parentId);
+  }
+  return path.reverse();
+}
+
+export function indexById<T extends SyncFields>(list: readonly T[]): Map<Id, T> {
+  return new Map(list.map((entity) => [entity.id, entity]));
+}
+
+/** Active children grouped by parent, each list sorted by `order` and then by id. */
+export function childrenIndex<T extends Node & { order?: number }>(
+  list: readonly T[],
+): Map<Id, T[]> {
+  const map = new Map<Id, T[]>();
+  for (const entity of list) {
+    if (!isActive(entity) || entity.parentId === null) continue;
+    const siblings = map.get(entity.parentId);
+    if (siblings) siblings.push(entity);
+    else map.set(entity.parentId, [entity]);
+  }
+  for (const siblings of map.values()) {
+    siblings.sort((a, b) => (a.order ?? 0) - (b.order ?? 0) || (a.id < b.id ? -1 : 1));
+  }
+  return map;
+}
+
+/** Every active descendant of an entity, at any depth. Safe on data that has a cycle. */
+export function descendantIds<T extends Node & { order?: number }>(
+  rootId: Id,
+  list: readonly T[],
+): Set<Id> {
+  const children = childrenIndex(list);
+  const found = new Set<Id>();
+  const stack = [rootId];
+  while (stack.length > 0) {
+    const current = stack.pop()!;
+    for (const child of children.get(current) ?? []) {
+      if (child.id === rootId || found.has(child.id)) continue;
+      found.add(child.id);
+      stack.push(child.id);
+    }
+  }
+  return found;
+}
+
+/** Whether giving an item that parent would put the item inside its own subtree. */
+export function wouldCreateCycle(
+  itemId: Id,
+  newParentId: Id | null,
+  items: readonly Item[],
+): boolean {
+  if (newParentId === null) return false;
+  if (newParentId === itemId) return true;
+  return descendantIds(itemId, items).has(newParentId);
+}

+export type Id = string;
+
+/** An instant in time, written as an ISO 8601 string in UTC, such as 2026-11-07T17:00:00.000Z. */
+export type Timestamp = string;
+
+/** A calendar date with no time and no time zone, written YYYY-MM-DD. */
+export type PlainDate = string;
+
+/** Fields carried by every entity, so that sync can be added later without migrating data. */
+export interface SyncFields {
+  /** A UUID generated on the device. */
+  id: Id;
+  createdAt: Timestamp;
+  updatedAt: Timestamp;
+  /** Empty while the entity exists. Deleting sets it instead of removing the record (tombstone). */
+  deletedAt: Timestamp | null;
+}
+
+export interface Agenda extends SyncFields {
+  name: string;
+  /** Base tone, for example #3b5bdb. Light and dark variants are derived. */
+  color: string;
+  order: number;
+}

+export interface AgendaGroup extends SyncFields {
+  name: string;
+  agendaIds: Id[];
+  order: number;
+}
+
+export type ItemKind = 'event' | 'task';
+
+/** The ways to arrange a day in the Timeline. Same values as `AgendaLayout` in `filters`. */
+export const SAVED_VIEW_LAYOUTS = ['mixed', 'separate', 'grouped'] as const;
+export type SavedViewLayout = (typeof SAVED_VIEW_LAYOUTS)[number];
+
+/** A whole-day schedule. It has no time zone: the 12th is the 12th wherever you are. */
+export interface AllDaySchedule {
+  allDay: true;
+  /** First day. */
+  start: PlainDate;
+  /** Last day, included. Empty means a single day. */
+  end?: PlainDate;
+}
+
+/** A schedule with a time of day, stored as absolute instants. */
+export interface TimedSchedule {
+  allDay: false;
+  start: Timestamp;
+  end?: Timestamp;
+  /** Optional IANA name (for example Europe/Lisbon) for items that belong to another city. */
+  timeZone?: string;
+}
+
+/** When something happens. Used by events and by work blocks, never by a task's own window. */
+export type Schedule = AllDaySchedule | TimedSchedule;
+
+/** A delivery that is due on a day, with no time of day. It has no time zone. */
+export interface AllDayDue {
+  allDay: true;
+  date: PlainDate;
+}

+/** A delivery with a deadline time, stored as an absolute instant. */

+  allDay: false;

+  /** Optional IANA name (for example America/Sao_Paulo) of the place the deadline refers to. */
+  timeZone?: string;
+}
+
+/** The delivery of a task: a whole day (the default) or a day and time. */
+export type Due = AllDayDue | TimedDue;
+
+export interface ItemLink {
+  label: string;
+  url: string;
+}
+
+export interface Item extends SyncFields {
+  parentId: Id | null;
+  /** Position among siblings. */
+  order: number;
+  kind: ItemKind;
+  title: string;
+  /** Free text with Markdown. */
+  notes: string;
+  /**
+   * When an event or a work block happens. Empty means unscheduled, which lives in the inbox.
+   * Tasks do not use it: they have a window (`from` and `due`) instead.
+   */
+  schedule: Schedule | null;
+  /**
+   * Tasks only. The first day the task is pending, such as the day a teacher assigned it.
+   * Empty means the day the task was created. Needs `due`.
+   */
+  from: PlainDate | null;
+  /** Tasks only. The delivery. The task is pending every day from `from` until it is done. */
+  due: Due | null;
+  agendaId: Id;
+  tagIds: Id[];
+  /**

+   * parent's parent while each one keeps this on. Only matters for an item that has a parent. Turn
+   * it off for a child that does not belong to its parent's projects.
+   */
+  inheritTags: boolean;
+  /** Required for tasks. Optional for events. */
+  statusId: Id | null;
+  location: string;
+  links: ItemLink[];
+}
+
+export interface Tag extends SyncFields {
+  name: string;
+  parentId: Id | null;
+  /** Empty means global. A filled list restricts the tag to those agendas. */
+  agendaIds: Id[];
+  color: string;
+}

+/** What the app understands about a status group. Names are free. */
+export type StatusRole = 'planned' | 'started' | 'done';
+
+export interface StatusGroup extends SyncFields {
+  name: string;
+  role: StatusRole;
+  order: number;
+}
+
+/** A status is also a Kanban column. */
+export interface Status extends SyncFields {
+  name: string;
+  groupId: Id;
+  order: number;
+}

+export type DayPeriod = 'dawn' | 'morning' | 'afternoon' | 'evening';
+
+/** Hours (0 to 24) where the morning, the afternoon and the evening start. Dawn starts at 0. */
+export interface PeriodBounds {
+  morningStart: number;
+  afternoonStart: number;
+  eveningStart: number;
+}

+export interface Settings {
+  /** An IANA name, or auto to follow the device. */
+  displayTimeZone: string;
+  periodBounds: PeriodBounds;

+/** A chip of the "when" filter: a day period, or `untimed` (whole-day events and task strips). */
+export type SavedViewPeriod = DayPeriod | 'untimed';

+/**
+ * The sieves of a saved view. It has the same shape as `ItemFilter` in `filters`, written out here
+ * because the core cannot import the layers above it. A test keeps the two in step.
+ */
+export interface SavedViewFilter {
+  tagIds: Id[];
+  kinds: ItemKind[];

+  dueWithinDays: number | null;

+/**
+ * What the person chose to see in the Timeline, saved under a name: the filter, which agendas are
+ * shown and how a day is laid out. It is plain data, so it syncs like everything else.

+export interface SavedView extends SyncFields {

+  order: number;
+  filter: SavedViewFilter;

+  agendaIds: Id[] | null;
+  layout: SavedViewLayout;
+}

+import { isPlainDate } from './plainDate';
+import { isTimestamp, validateSchedule, type ScheduleIssue } from './schedule';
+import { dueDate } from './window';
+import { isValidTimeZone } from './zone';
+import type { Due, Item } from './types';
+
+export type DueIssue = 'invalidDueDate' | 'invalidDueInstant' | 'invalidDueTimeZone';
+
+export type ItemIssue =
+  | 'titleRequired'
+  | 'taskNeedsStatus'
+  | 'parentIsSelf'
+  | 'taskCannotHaveSchedule'
+  | 'eventCannotHaveWindow'
+  | 'fromNeedsDue'
+  | 'invalidFromDate'
+  | 'fromAfterDue'
+  | DueIssue
+  | ScheduleIssue;
+
+export function validateDue(due: Due): DueIssue[] {
+  if (due.allDay) return isPlainDate(due.date) ? [] : ['invalidDueDate'];
+  if (!isTimestamp(due.at)) return ['invalidDueInstant'];
+  if (due.timeZone !== undefined && !isValidTimeZone(due.timeZone)) return ['invalidDueTimeZone'];
+  return [];
+}
+
+/**
+ * Checks one item. The display time zone is optional: it is only needed to compare a start day
+ * with a timed delivery, because the day of that delivery is the day in the display zone (the
+ * same rule the window uses). Without a zone that one comparison is skipped.
+ */
+export function validateItem(item: Item, displayTimeZone?: string): ItemIssue[] {
+  const issues: ItemIssue[] = [];
+  if (item.title.trim() === '') issues.push('titleRequired');
+  if (item.kind === 'task' && item.statusId === null) issues.push('taskNeedsStatus');
+  if (item.parentId === item.id) issues.push('parentIsSelf');
+
+  if (item.kind === 'task' && item.schedule !== null) issues.push('taskCannotHaveSchedule');
+  if (item.kind === 'event' && (item.from !== null || item.due !== null)) {
+    issues.push('eventCannotHaveWindow');
+  }
+  if (item.schedule) issues.push(...validateSchedule(item.schedule));
+
+  if (item.due) issues.push(...validateDue(item.due));
+  if (item.from !== null) {
+    if (item.due === null) issues.push('fromNeedsDue');
+    if (!isPlainDate(item.from)) issues.push('invalidFromDate');
+  }
+
+  if (
+    item.from !== null &&
+    item.due !== null &&
+    isPlainDate(item.from) &&
+    validateDue(item.due).length === 0
+  ) {
+    const zone = item.due.allDay ? 'UTC' : displayTimeZone;
+    if (zone !== undefined && item.from > dueDate(item.due, zone)) issues.push('fromAfterDue');
+  }
+  return issues;
+}

+import { isActive } from './entities';
+import { comparePlainDates } from './plainDate';
+import { timestampToMs } from './schedule';
+import { localDate } from './zone';
+import type { Due, Id, Item, PlainDate, Timestamp } from './types';
+
+/*
+ * The window of a task: the days when it counts as pending.
+ * Analogy: a teacher hands out an assignment on the 3rd and it is due on the 24th. From the 3rd
+ * to the 24th it sits on your desk, so you should see it on every one of those days, and not
+ * only on the day you hand it in.
+ */
+
+export interface TaskWindow {
+  /** First day the task is pending. */
+  from: PlainDate;
+  /** Last day, which is the delivery day. */
+  due: PlainDate;
+}
+
+/**
+ * The calendar day of a delivery. A whole-day delivery is that date. A timed delivery is the
+ * day it falls on in the display zone, so it sits on the same day as everything else on screen.
+ */
+export function dueDate(due: Due, displayTimeZone: string): PlainDate {
+  return due.allDay ? due.date : localDate(timestampToMs(due.at), displayTimeZone);
+}
+
+/**
+ * The window of a task, or null for an item with no delivery (events and tasks in the inbox).
+ * Without a start, the window begins on the day the task was created. A task created after its
+ * own delivery day gets a window of just that one day, so it is not hidden.
+ */
+export function taskWindow(item: Item, displayTimeZone: string): TaskWindow | null {
+  if (item.kind !== 'task' || item.due === null) return null;
+  const due = dueDate(item.due, displayTimeZone);
+  if (item.from !== null) return { from: item.from, due };
+
+  const created = localDate(timestampToMs(item.createdAt), displayTimeZone);
+  return { from: comparePlainDates(created, due) < 0 ? created : due, due };
+}
+
+/** Whether a calendar day falls inside the window of the task, both ends included. */
+export function isInWindow(item: Item, date: PlainDate, displayTimeZone: string): boolean {
+  const window = taskWindow(item, displayTimeZone);
+  if (!window) return false;
+  return comparePlainDates(date, window.from) >= 0 && comparePlainDates(date, window.due) <= 0;
+}
+
+/** Whether the delivery time has passed. A whole-day delivery passes when its day is over. */
+export function isPastDue(due: Due, now: Timestamp, displayTimeZone: string): boolean {
+  const nowMs = timestampToMs(now);
+  if (!due.allDay) return nowMs > timestampToMs(due.at);
+  return comparePlainDates(localDate(nowMs, displayTimeZone), due.date) > 0;
+}
+
+/**
+ * The tasks that are pending on one day: inside their window and not done. Deleted items are
+ * ignored. A task whose delivery day has passed is not here, it belongs to the overdue strip.
+ */
+export function pendingOnDate(
+  items: readonly Item[],
+  date: PlainDate,
+  displayTimeZone: string,
+  doneIds: ReadonlySet<Id>,
+): Item[] {
+  return items.filter(
+    (item) =>
+      isActive(item) &&
+      !(item.statusId !== null && doneIds.has(item.statusId)) &&
+      isInWindow(item, date, displayTimeZone),
+  );
+}
+
+/** The tasks whose delivery has passed and that are not done, oldest delivery first. */
+export function overdueTasks(
+  items: readonly Item[],
+  now: Timestamp,
+  displayTimeZone: string,
+  doneIds: ReadonlySet<Id>,
+): Item[] {
+  const late = items.filter(
+    (item) =>
+      isActive(item) &&
+      item.kind === 'task' &&
+      item.due !== null &&
+      !(item.statusId !== null && doneIds.has(item.statusId)) &&
+      isPastDue(item.due, now, displayTimeZone),
+  );
+  const key = (item: Item) => dueDate(item.due!, displayTimeZone);
+  return late.sort((a, b) => comparePlainDates(key(a), key(b)) || (a.id < b.id ? -1 : 1));
+}
+
+/**
+ * The work blocks of a task: timed events placed directly under it, in time order. A work block
+ * is time reserved to take care of the task. It is an ordinary event, so it shows in the calendar
+ * and the timeline at its own hour, and it never changes the progress of the task.
+ */
+export function workBlocks(task: Item, items: readonly Item[]): Item[] {
+  return items
+    .filter(
+      (item) =>
+        isActive(item) &&
+        item.parentId === task.id &&
+        item.kind === 'event' &&
+        item.schedule !== null &&
+        !item.schedule.allDay,
+    )
+    .sort((a, b) => {
+      const aMs = timestampToMs((a.schedule as { start: Timestamp }).start);
+      const bMs = timestampToMs((b.schedule as { start: Timestamp }).start);
+      return aMs - bMs || (a.id < b.id ? -1 : 1);
+    });
+}

+import { formatPlainDate, parsePlainDate } from './plainDate';
+import type { PlainDate } from './types';
+
+/*
+ * Time zone rules, built on the Intl support that browsers and Node already have.
+ * Nothing in the core reads the device clock zone by itself: every function that needs a zone
+ * receives it as a parameter. That keeps the rules pure and easy to test.
+ */
+
+const formatters = new Map<string, Intl.DateTimeFormat>();
+
+function formatterFor(timeZone: string): Intl.DateTimeFormat {
+  let formatter = formatters.get(timeZone);
+  if (!formatter) {
+    // Throws a RangeError for an unknown zone, before anything is cached
+    formatter = new Intl.DateTimeFormat('en-US', {
+      timeZone,
+      hourCycle: 'h23',
+      year: 'numeric',
+      month: '2-digit',
+      day: '2-digit',
+      hour: '2-digit',
+      minute: '2-digit',
+      second: '2-digit',
+    });
+    formatters.set(timeZone, formatter);
+  }
+  return formatter;
+}
+
+export function isValidTimeZone(value: unknown): value is string {
+  if (typeof value !== 'string' || value === '') return false;
+  try {
+    formatterFor(value);
+    return true;
+  } catch {
+    return false;
+  }
+}
+
+export function deviceTimeZone(): string {
+  const zone = Intl.DateTimeFormat().resolvedOptions().timeZone;
+  return isValidTimeZone(zone) ? zone : 'UTC';
+}
+
+export interface ZonedParts {
+  year: number;
+  month: number;
+  day: number;
+  hour: number;
+  minute: number;
+  second: number;
+}
+
+/** The wall clock reading in a zone, for an absolute instant given in milliseconds. */
+export function getZonedParts(ms: number, timeZone: string): ZonedParts {
+  const parts = formatterFor(timeZone).formatToParts(new Date(ms));
+  const read = (type: string) => Number(parts.find((part) => part.type === type)?.value);
+  return {
+    year: read('year'),
+    month: read('month'),
+    day: read('day'),
+    hour: read('hour'),
+    minute: read('minute'),
+    second: read('second'),
+  };
+}
+
+/** How far the zone is ahead of UTC at that instant, in milliseconds. */
+function offsetMs(ms: number, timeZone: string): number {
+  const whole = Math.floor(ms / 1000) * 1000;
+  const p = getZonedParts(whole, timeZone);
+  const asIfUtc = Date.UTC(p.year, p.month - 1, p.day, p.hour, p.minute, p.second);
+  return asIfUtc - whole;
+}
+
+export function getTimeZoneOffsetMinutes(ms: number, timeZone: string): number {
+  return offsetMs(ms, timeZone) / 60_000;
+}
+
+/** The calendar date it is in that zone at that instant. */
+export function localDate(ms: number, timeZone: string): PlainDate {
+  const { year, month, day } = getZonedParts(ms, timeZone);
+  return formatPlainDate({ year, month, day });
+}
+
+/**
+ * Turns a wall clock reading in a zone into an absolute instant, in milliseconds.
+ * Two edge cases around daylight saving time:
+ * - A reading that does not exist (the clock jumped forward) moves forward by the gap.
+ * - A reading that happens twice (the clock went back) resolves to the first occurrence.
+ */
+export function zonedTimeToMs(
+  date: PlainDate,
+  hour: number,
+  minute: number,
+  timeZone: string,
+): number {
+  const parts = parsePlainDate(date);
+  if (!parts) throw new RangeError(`Invalid date: ${date}`);
+  const asIfUtc = Date.UTC(parts.year, parts.month - 1, parts.day, hour, minute);
+
+  const firstOffset = offsetMs(asIfUtc, timeZone);
+  const first = asIfUtc - firstOffset;
+  const secondOffset = offsetMs(first, timeZone);
+  if (secondOffset === firstOffset) return first;
+
+  const second = asIfUtc - secondOffset;
+  if (offsetMs(second, timeZone) === secondOffset) return second;
+
+  // The reading falls in a gap
+  return Math.max(first, second);
+}
+
+/** The instant a calendar day begins in a zone. */
+export function startOfDayMs(date: PlainDate, timeZone: string): number {
+  return zonedTimeToMs(date, 0, 0, timeZone);
+}
+
+/** Resolves the setting (a zone name or auto) into a real zone name. */
+export function resolveTimeZone(setting: string, device: string = deviceTimeZone()): string {
+  if (setting === 'auto') return device;
+  return isValidTimeZone(setting) ? setting : device;
+}

+import {
+  isActive,
+  tagsForFilter,
+  type Agenda,
+  type AgendaGroup,
+  type FilterTag,
+  type Id,
+  type Item,
+  type Tag,
+} from '../core';
+import type { ItemFilter } from './types';
+
+/*
+ * Which agendas the person wants to see. Analogy: a row of light switches, one per agenda, plus a
+ * master switch per group that flips all the switches of its agendas at once.
+ *
+ * It is plain data (a list of ids or null), so a saved view can store it as JSON later.
+ *
+ * - `null` means every agenda, including the ones created later. This is the default, so a new
+ *   agenda shows up by itself.
+ * - A list means exactly those agendas. An empty list is allowed: the person hid everything.
+ *
+ * Agendas that were deleted are ignored when the list is read, so deleting an agenda never leaves
+ * a selection that points at nothing. If every agenda the list named is gone, the selection falls
+ * back to showing everything, instead of leaving a screen that is empty for no visible reason.
+ */
+export type AgendaSelection = Id[] | null;
+
+export const ALL_AGENDAS: AgendaSelection = null;
+
+/** The shown state of a group: all its agendas, only some of them, or none. */
+export type GroupState = 'all' | 'some' | 'none';
+
+/** The order the agendas have in the app: by `order`, then by name, then by id. */
+export function compareAgendas(a: Agenda, b: Agenda): number {
+  return (
+    a.order - b.order || a.name.localeCompare(b.name) || (a.id < b.id ? -1 : a.id > b.id ? 1 : 0)
+  );
+}
+
+function activeAgendas(agendas: readonly Agenda[]): Agenda[] {
+  return agendas.filter(isActive).sort(compareAgendas);
+}
+
+/** The ids of the agendas that are shown, in the order of the agendas. */
+export function visibleAgendaIds(selection: AgendaSelection, agendas: readonly Agenda[]): Id[] {
+  const active = activeAgendas(agendas);
+  if (selection === null) return active.map((agenda) => agenda.id);
+  const chosen = new Set(selection);
+  const kept = active.filter((agenda) => chosen.has(agenda.id));
+  if (kept.length === 0 && selection.length > 0) return active.map((agenda) => agenda.id);
+  return kept.map((agenda) => agenda.id);
+}
+
+/** True when some agenda is hidden, so the interface can say that something is filtered out. */
+export function isAgendaSelectionActive(
+  selection: AgendaSelection,
+  agendas: readonly Agenda[],
+): boolean {
+  return visibleAgendaIds(selection, agendas).length < activeAgendas(agendas).length;
+}
+
+/** Turns a set of shown agendas into a selection. Showing all of them is `null` (the default). */
+function toSelection(shown: ReadonlySet<Id>, active: readonly Agenda[]): AgendaSelection {
+  if (active.every((agenda) => shown.has(agenda.id))) return null;
+  return active.filter((agenda) => shown.has(agenda.id)).map((agenda) => agenda.id);
+}
+
+/** Shows exactly these agendas. Unknown and deleted ids are ignored. */
+export function selectAgendas(ids: readonly Id[], agendas: readonly Agenda[]): AgendaSelection {
+  return toSelection(new Set(ids), activeAgendas(agendas));
+}
+
+/** Shows an agenda that is hidden, or hides one that is shown. An unknown id changes nothing. */
+export function toggleAgenda(
+  selection: AgendaSelection,
+  agendaId: Id,
+  agendas: readonly Agenda[],
+): AgendaSelection {
+  const active = activeAgendas(agendas);
+  if (!active.some((agenda) => agenda.id === agendaId)) return selection;
+  const shown = new Set(visibleAgendaIds(selection, agendas));
+  if (shown.has(agendaId)) shown.delete(agendaId);
+  else shown.add(agendaId);
+  return toSelection(shown, active);
+}
+
+/** The agendas of a group that still exist, without repeats. */
+function groupMembers(group: AgendaGroup, active: readonly Agenda[]): Id[] {
+  const members = new Set(group.agendaIds);
+  return active.filter((agenda) => members.has(agenda.id)).map((agenda) => agenda.id);
+}
+
+/** Whether all, some or none of the group's agendas are shown. A group with no agenda is none. */
+export function groupState(
+  group: AgendaGroup,
+  selection: AgendaSelection,
+  agendas: readonly Agenda[],
+): GroupState {
+  const members = groupMembers(group, activeAgendas(agendas));
+  if (members.length === 0) return 'none';
+  const shown = new Set(visibleAgendaIds(selection, agendas));
+  const count = members.filter((id) => shown.has(id)).length;
+  if (count === 0) return 'none';
+  return count === members.length ? 'all' : 'some';
+}
+
+/**
+ * One action for the whole group. When all its agendas are shown it hides them. Otherwise (some or
+ * none shown) it shows them all. An agenda that belongs to two groups follows whichever group was
+ * used last. A group with no agenda changes nothing.
+ */
+export function toggleGroup(
+  selection: AgendaSelection,
+  group: AgendaGroup,
+  agendas: readonly Agenda[],
+): AgendaSelection {
+  const active = activeAgendas(agendas);
+  const members = groupMembers(group, active);
+  if (members.length === 0) return selection;
+  const hide = groupState(group, selection, agendas) === 'all';
+  const shown = new Set(visibleAgendaIds(selection, agendas));
+  for (const id of members) {
+    if (hide) shown.delete(id);
+    else shown.add(id);
+  }
+  return toSelection(shown, active);
+}
+
+/**
+ * The items that belong to a shown agenda, in the same order. Returns the same list when the
+ * selection is `null`. Inherited tags are found by looking at the parents, so run the tag, type and
+ * text sieves (`filterItems`) on the whole list first and cut by agenda after. That way a child
+ * still counts the tags of a parent that sits in a hidden agenda.
+ */
+export function filterByAgendas(
+  items: readonly Item[],
+  selection: AgendaSelection,
+  agendas: readonly Agenda[],
+): readonly Item[] {
+  if (selection === null) return items;
+  const shown = new Set(visibleAgendaIds(selection, agendas));
+  return items.filter((item) => shown.has(item.agendaId));
+}
+
+/**
+ * The tags the filter offers for the shown agendas: the ones valid in at least one of them, with
+ * `partial` set for the ones that exist in only part of the selection. When every agenda is hidden
+ * there is nothing to narrow by, so all tags are offered.
+ */
+export function tagsForSelection(
+  tags: readonly Tag[],
+  selection: AgendaSelection,
+  agendas: readonly Agenda[],
+): FilterTag[] {
+  const shown = visibleAgendaIds(selection, agendas);
+  if (shown.length === 0) return tags.filter(isActive).map((tag) => ({ tag, partial: false }));
+  return tagsForFilter(tags, shown);
+}
+
+/**
+ * Takes out of the tag filter the tags that are not offered for the shown agendas any more (for
+ * example the tag of an agenda that was just hidden), so the filter never waits for a tag that can
+ * not be unticked in the panel. Returns those tags, to tell the person, and the same filter object
+ * when nothing was taken out.
+ */
+export function dropUnavailableTags(
+  filter: ItemFilter,
+  tags: readonly Tag[],
+  selection: AgendaSelection,
+  agendas: readonly Agenda[],
+): { filter: ItemFilter; dropped: Tag[] } {
+  const offered = new Set(tagsForSelection(tags, selection, agendas).map((entry) => entry.tag.id));
+  const active = new Map(tags.filter(isActive).map((tag) => [tag.id, tag]));
+  const dropped = filter.tagIds
+    .filter((id) => active.has(id) && !offered.has(id))
+    .map((id) => active.get(id)!);
+  if (dropped.length === 0) return { filter, dropped };
+  const gone = new Set(dropped.map((tag) => tag.id));
+  return { filter: { ...filter, tagIds: filter.tagIds.filter((id) => !gone.has(id)) }, dropped };
+}

+import {
+  DEFAULT_PERIOD_BOUNDS,
+  daysBetween,
+  periodsOnDate,
+  type DayPeriod,
+  type OverdueEntry,
+  type PeriodBounds,
+  type TimelineDay,
+} from '../core';
+import { isValidDueWithin, type ItemFilter } from './types';
+
+/** The chosen day periods, and whether the "untimed" chip is on. Null means the sieve is off. */
+function chosenPeriods(filter: ItemFilter): { periods: Set<DayPeriod>; untimed: boolean } | null {
+  if (filter.periods.length === 0) return null;
+  const periods = new Set<DayPeriod>();
+  let untimed = false;
+  for (const chip of filter.periods) {
+    if (chip === 'untimed') untimed = true;
+    else periods.add(chip);
+  }
+  return { periods, untimed };
+}
+
+/**
+ * The sieves that depend on the day, applied to one Timeline day that was already built from the
+ * items that passed `filterItems`:
+ * - periods ("any of these" chips): a timed event stays only if it touches a chosen day period on
+ *   that day. Whole-day events and open tasks have no set time, so they stay only when the
+ *   `untimed` chip is on.
+ * - due within: an open task stays only when its delivery is at most that many days after the day
+ *   being shown, so a task given months ahead does not fill every day until it gets close.
+ * The `empty` flag is recomputed, so a day that lost everything can fold. Returns the same day
+ * object when nothing changes.
+ */
+export function applyDayFilters(
+  day: TimelineDay,
+  filter: ItemFilter,
+  timeZone: string,
+  bounds: PeriodBounds = DEFAULT_PERIOD_BOUNDS,
+): TimelineDay {
+  const chosen = chosenPeriods(filter);
+  const limit = filter.dueWithinDays;
+  const useLimit = isValidDueWithin(limit);
+  if (chosen === null && !useLimit) return day;
+
+  const keepUntimed = chosen === null || chosen.untimed;
+  const allDay = keepUntimed ? day.allDay : [];
+  const timed =
+    chosen === null
+      ? day.timed
+      : day.timed.filter((entry) =>
+          periodsOnDate(entry.item.schedule, day.date, timeZone, bounds).some((period) =>
+            chosen.periods.has(period),
+          ),
+        );
+  let open = keepUntimed ? day.open : [];
+  if (useLimit) open = open.filter((task) => daysBetween(day.date, task.dueDate) <= limit);
+
+  return { ...day, allDay, timed, open, empty: allDay.length + timed.length + open.length === 0 };
+}
+
+/**
+ * The overdue strip under the period chips: it has no time of day, so it stays only when no chip is
+ * on or the `untimed` chip is on. The "due within" limit never cuts it. Returns the same list when
+ * nothing changes.
+ */
+export function applyOverdueFilter(entries: OverdueEntry[], filter: ItemFilter): OverdueEntry[] {
+  const chosen = chosenPeriods(filter);
+  return chosen === null || chosen.untimed ? entries : [];
+}

+import {
+  effectiveTagIds,
+  indexById,
+  isActive,
+  tagWithDescendantIds,
+  type Id,
+  type Item,
+  type Tag,
+} from '../core';
+import { containsAllWords, searchWords } from './text';
+import type { ItemFilter } from './types';
+
+/**
+ * The tags a filter really uses: the selected ones that still exist (deleted or unknown tags are
+ * dropped, so deleting a tag never leaves a filter that matches nothing), each with its
+ * descendants. Null means the tag sieve is off.
+ */
+export function expandedTagIds(filter: ItemFilter, tags: readonly Tag[]): Set<Id> | null {
+  const active = tags.filter(isActive);
+  const byId = indexById(active);
+  const selected = filter.tagIds.filter((id) => byId.has(id));
+  if (selected.length === 0) return null;
+  const result = new Set<Id>();
+  for (const id of selected) {
+    for (const found of tagWithDescendantIds(id, active)) result.add(found);
+  }
+  return result;
+}
+
+/**
+ * A function that says whether one item passes the tag, kind and text sieves. The periods and the
+ * "due within" limit depend on the day, so they live in `applyDayFilters`.
+ * Build it once and reuse it for every item.
+ *
+ * `items` is every item the parents can be found in, because an item also counts as having the
+ * tags it inherits from its parent (`inheritTags`). Without it, only the item's own tags count.
+ */
+export function createItemMatcher(
+  filter: ItemFilter,
+  tags: readonly Tag[],
+  items: readonly Item[] = [],
+): (item: Item) => boolean {
+  const tagIds = expandedTagIds(filter, tags);
+  const byId = indexById(items.filter(isActive));
+  const kinds = new Set(filter.kinds);
+  const words = searchWords(filter.text);
+
+  return (item) => {
+    if (kinds.size > 0 && !kinds.has(item.kind)) return false;
+    if (tagIds !== null && !effectiveTagIds(item, byId).some((id) => tagIds.has(id))) return false;
+    if (words.length > 0) {
+      return containsAllWords(`${item.title} ${item.notes} ${item.location}`, words);
+    }
+    return true;
+  };
+}
+
+/**
+ * The items that pass the tag, kind and text sieves, in the same order. Inherited tags are found
+ * among `items`, so pass the whole list, not one already narrowed.
+ */
+export function filterItems(
+  items: readonly Item[],
+  filter: ItemFilter,
+  tags: readonly Tag[],
+): Item[] {
+  const matches = createItemMatcher(filter, tags, items);
+  return items.filter(matches);
+}
diff --git a/src/filters/layout.ts b/src/filters/layout.ts
new file mode 100644

+import {
+  isActive,
+  type Agenda,
+  type AgendaGroup,
+  type Id,
+  type OverdueEntry,
+  type TimelineDay,
+} from '../core';
+import { compareAgendas } from './agendas';
+
+/*
+ * How the shown agendas are laid out inside each day. Analogy: one pile of cards per day, or the
+ * same cards dealt into a pile per agenda, or into a pile per group of agendas.
+ *
+ * - `mixed`: one list per day, all agendas together, in time order (what the Timeline did so far).
+ * - `separate`: one section per agenda, in the order of the agendas.
+ * - `grouped`: one section per agenda group, in the order of the groups, plus a last section for
+ *   the agendas that are in no group. An agenda listed in two groups goes to the first of them
+ *   (by group order), so an item is never shown twice.
+ *
+ * Inside a section the order is the one the day already had (time order). A section with nothing
+ * in it is never returned, and a day with nothing returns no section at all.
+ *
+ * Like the selection, the layout is a plain string, so a saved view can store it.
+ */
+export type AgendaLayout = 'mixed' | 'separate' | 'grouped';
+
+export const DEFAULT_LAYOUT: AgendaLayout = 'mixed';
+
+export const AGENDA_LAYOUTS: readonly AgendaLayout[] = ['mixed', 'separate', 'grouped'];
+
+export function isAgendaLayout(value: unknown): value is AgendaLayout {
+  return typeof value === 'string' && (AGENDA_LAYOUTS as readonly string[]).includes(value);
+}
+
+export type SectionKind = 'all' | 'agenda' | 'group' | 'ungrouped';
+
+/** What a section is, so the screen can write its title. The names come from the entities. */
+export interface SectionInfo {
+  /** Stable, to use as a React key and to remember which sections are folded. */
+  key: string;
+  kind: SectionKind;
+  /** Set for `agenda` sections. */
+  agendaId: Id | null;
+  /** Set for `group` sections. */
+  groupId: Id | null;
+}
+
+export interface DaySection {
+  info: SectionInfo;
+  day: TimelineDay;
+}
+
+export interface OverdueSection {
+  info: SectionInfo;
+  entries: OverdueEntry[];
+}
+
+/** The sections of a layout and the rule that sends an agenda to one of them. Build it once. */
+export interface LayoutPlan {
+  layout: AgendaLayout;
+  /** The sections in the order they are shown. In `mixed` there is only the `all` one. */
+  sections: readonly SectionInfo[];
+  /** The key of the section an agenda belongs to. */
+  keyOf: (agendaId: Id) => string;
+}
+
+const ALL_SECTION: SectionInfo = { key: 'all', kind: 'all', agendaId: null, groupId: null };
+const UNGROUPED_SECTION: SectionInfo = {
+  key: 'ungrouped',
+  kind: 'ungrouped',
+  agendaId: null,
+  groupId: null,
+};
+
+const agendaKey = (agendaId: Id) => `agenda:${agendaId}`;
+const groupKey = (groupId: Id) => `group:${groupId}`;
+
+function compareGroups(a: AgendaGroup, b: AgendaGroup): number {
+  return (
+    a.order - b.order || a.name.localeCompare(b.name) || (a.id < b.id ? -1 : a.id > b.id ? 1 : 0)
+  );
+}
+
+/**
+ * Builds the plan for a layout. Pass every agenda (the plan only shows the sections that have
+ * something in them, so hidden agendas never show up). Deleted agendas and groups are ignored.
+ */
+export function createLayoutPlan(
+  layout: AgendaLayout,
+  agendas: readonly Agenda[],
+  groups: readonly AgendaGroup[],
+): LayoutPlan {
+  if (layout === 'separate') {
+    return {
+      layout,
+      sections: agendas
+        .filter(isActive)
+        .sort(compareAgendas)
+        .map((agenda) => ({
+          key: agendaKey(agenda.id),
+          kind: 'agenda' as const,
+          agendaId: agenda.id,
+          groupId: null,
+        })),
+      keyOf: agendaKey,
+    };
+  }
+
+  if (layout === 'grouped') {
+    const active = groups.filter(isActive).sort(compareGroups);
+    const owner = new Map<Id, Id>();
+    for (const group of active) {
+      for (const agendaId of group.agendaIds) {
+        if (!owner.has(agendaId)) owner.set(agendaId, group.id);
+      }
+    }
+    return {
+      layout,
+      sections: [
+        ...active.map((group) => ({
+          key: groupKey(group.id),
+          kind: 'group' as const,
+          agendaId: null,
+          groupId: group.id,
+        })),
+        UNGROUPED_SECTION,
+      ],
+      keyOf: (agendaId) => {
+        const groupId = owner.get(agendaId);
+        return groupId === undefined ? UNGROUPED_SECTION.key : groupKey(groupId);
+      },
+    };
+  }
+
+  return { layout: 'mixed', sections: [ALL_SECTION], keyOf: () => ALL_SECTION.key };
+}
+
+/** Splits a list into one list per section key, keeping the order inside each. */
+function partition<T>(
+  entries: readonly T[],
+  agendaIdOf: (entry: T) => Id,
+  plan: LayoutPlan,
+): Map<string, T[]> {
+  const buckets = new Map<string, T[]>();
+  for (const entry of entries) {
+    const key = plan.keyOf(agendaIdOf(entry));
+    const bucket = buckets.get(key);
+    if (bucket) bucket.push(entry);
+    else buckets.set(key, [entry]);
+  }
+  return buckets;
+}
+
+/**
+ * The sections that have something, in plan order. A key the plan does not know (an item whose
+ * agenda is missing from the list) still gets a section, after the known ones, as an agenda.
+ */
+function usedSections(plan: LayoutPlan, keys: ReadonlySet<string>): SectionInfo[] {
+  const known = new Set(plan.sections.map((info) => info.key));
+  const strays = [...keys].filter((key) => !known.has(key)).sort();
+  return [
+    ...plan.sections.filter((info) => keys.has(info.key)),
+    ...strays.map((key) => ({
+      key,
+      kind: 'agenda' as const,
+      agendaId: key.startsWith('agenda:') ? key.slice('agenda:'.length) : null,
+      groupId: null,
+    })),
+  ];
+}
+
+/** One day dealt into sections. In `mixed` it is the day itself, or nothing when the day is empty. */
+export function arrangeDay(day: TimelineDay, plan: LayoutPlan): DaySection[] {
+  if (day.empty) return [];
+  if (plan.layout === 'mixed') return [{ info: ALL_SECTION, day }];
+
+  const allDay = partition(day.allDay, (entry) => entry.item.agendaId, plan);
+  const timed = partition(day.timed, (entry) => entry.item.agendaId, plan);
+  const open = partition(day.open, (task) => task.item.agendaId, plan);
+  const keys = new Set([...allDay.keys(), ...timed.keys(), ...open.keys()]);
+
+  return usedSections(plan, keys).map((info) => {
+    const part = {
+      date: day.date,
+      allDay: allDay.get(info.key) ?? [],
+      timed: timed.get(info.key) ?? [],
+      open: open.get(info.key) ?? [],
+    };
+    return { info, day: { ...part, empty: false } };
+  });
+}
+
+/** The overdue strip dealt into sections, with the same rules as `arrangeDay`. */
+export function arrangeOverdue(entries: OverdueEntry[], plan: LayoutPlan): OverdueSection[] {
+  if (entries.length === 0) return [];
+  if (plan.layout === 'mixed') return [{ info: ALL_SECTION, entries }];
+
+  const buckets = partition(entries, (entry) => entry.item.agendaId, plan);
+  return usedSections(plan, new Set(buckets.keys())).map((info) => ({
+    info,
+    entries: buckets.get(info.key) ?? [],
+  }));
+}
+
+/** One section of a day with its overdue entries too. Used for today, which carries the strip. */
+export interface CombinedSection {
+  info: SectionInfo;
+  /** What the day has in this section. Empty lists when only overdue entries belong here. */
+  day: TimelineDay;
+  /** The overdue entries of this section. Empty when none. */
+  overdue: OverdueEntry[];
+}
+
+/**
+ * A day and its overdue strip dealt into the same sections, in plan order. A section appears when
+ * the day or the strip has something for it, so an agenda that only has an overdue task still gets
+ * its section. Nothing at all (an empty day and no overdue entries) returns no section. In `mixed`
+ * the only section holds the day itself, untouched.
+ */
+export function arrangeDayWithOverdue(
+  day: TimelineDay,
+  overdue: OverdueEntry[],
+  plan: LayoutPlan,
+): CombinedSection[] {
+  const daySections = new Map(arrangeDay(day, plan).map((section) => [section.info.key, section]));
+  const overdueSections = new Map(
+    arrangeOverdue(overdue, plan).map((section) => [section.info.key, section]),
+  );
+  const keys = new Set([...daySections.keys(), ...overdueSections.keys()]);
+
+  return usedSections(plan, keys).map((info) => ({
+    info,
+    day: daySections.get(info.key)?.day ?? {
+      date: day.date,
+      allDay: [],
+      timed: [],
+      open: [],
+      empty: day.empty,
+    },
+    overdue: overdueSections.get(info.key)?.entries ?? [],
+  }));
+}

+import {
+  isActive,
+  type Agenda,
+  type Id,
+  type SavedView,
+  type SavedViewFilter,
+  type SavedViewLayout,
+} from '../core';
+import { ALL_AGENDAS, visibleAgendaIds, type AgendaSelection } from './agendas';
+import { DEFAULT_LAYOUT, type AgendaLayout } from './layout';
+import { EMPTY_FILTER, isValidDueWithin, type ItemFilter } from './types';
+
+/*
+ * What a saved view stores, seen from the screen. Analogy: a photo of the control panel. The panel
+ * has three groups of switches (the sieves, which agendas are shown and how a day is laid out).
+ * Saving a view takes a photo, applying one sets every switch back to the photo, and "changed"
+ * means the switches no longer match it.
+ *
+ * Everything here is plain data in and out, with no React and no storage.
+ */
+
+/** The three groups of switches of the Timeline. */
+export interface TimelineControls {
+  filter: ItemFilter;
+  selection: AgendaSelection;
+  layout: AgendaLayout;
+}
+
+/** The controls with nothing filtered, every agenda shown and the days mixed. */
+export const DEFAULT_CONTROLS: TimelineControls = {
+  filter: EMPTY_FILTER,
+  selection: ALL_AGENDAS,
+  layout: DEFAULT_LAYOUT,
+};
+
+/** The part of a saved view that comes from the controls (the rest is name and position). */
+export interface ViewSnapshot {
+  filter: SavedViewFilter;
+  agendaIds: Id[] | null;
+  layout: SavedViewLayout;
+}
+
+/** The longest name a saved view can have. */
+export const VIEW_NAME_MAX = 80;
+
+/** Takes the photo. The lists are copied, so changing the controls later never changes a view. */
+export function snapshotControls(controls: TimelineControls): ViewSnapshot {
+  const { filter, selection, layout } = controls;
+  return {
+    filter: {
+      tagIds: [...filter.tagIds],
+      kinds: [...filter.kinds],
+      periods: [...filter.periods],
+      text: filter.text,
+      dueWithinDays: filter.dueWithinDays,
+    },
+    agendaIds: selection === null ? null : [...selection],
+    layout,
+  };
+}
+
+/** Sets the controls back to a saved view. The lists are copied. */
+export function controlsFromView(view: SavedView): TimelineControls {
+  return {
+    filter: {
+      tagIds: [...view.filter.tagIds],
+      kinds: [...view.filter.kinds],
+      periods: [...view.filter.periods],
+      text: view.filter.text,
+      dueWithinDays: view.filter.dueWithinDays,
+    },
+    selection: view.agendaIds === null ? ALL_AGENDAS : [...view.agendaIds],
+    layout: view.layout,
+  };
+}
+
+function sameSet<T>(a: readonly T[], b: readonly T[]): boolean {
+  const left = new Set(a);
+  const right = new Set(b);
+  return left.size === right.size && [...left].every((value) => right.has(value));
+}
+
+/** A limit that does not count (empty, negative, decimal) is the same as no limit. */
+function dueLimit(value: number | null): number | null {
+  return isValidDueWithin(value) ? value : null;
+}
+
+/**
+ * True when the controls still show exactly what the view saved. The order of the ticked boxes does
+ * not matter, and the agendas are compared by what is shown: "every agenda" and a list naming all
+ * the agendas that exist look the same on the screen, so they count as the same.
+ */
+export function isViewCurrent(
+  view: SavedView,
+  controls: TimelineControls,
+  agendas: readonly Agenda[],
+): boolean {
+  const saved = controlsFromView(view);
+  return (
+    view.layout === controls.layout &&
+    sameSet(saved.filter.tagIds, controls.filter.tagIds) &&
+    sameSet(saved.filter.kinds, controls.filter.kinds) &&
+    sameSet(saved.filter.periods, controls.filter.periods) &&
+    saved.filter.text.trim() === controls.filter.text.trim() &&
+    dueLimit(saved.filter.dueWithinDays) === dueLimit(controls.filter.dueWithinDays) &&
+    sameSet(
+      visibleAgendaIds(saved.selection, agendas),
+      visibleAgendaIds(controls.selection, agendas),
+    )
+  );
+}
+
+/** Active views in the order they are listed: by `order`, then by name, then by id. */
+export function sortSavedViews(views: readonly SavedView[], locale?: string): SavedView[] {
+  return views
+    .filter(isActive)
+    .sort(
+      (a, b) =>
+        a.order - b.order ||
+        a.name.localeCompare(b.name, locale) ||
+        (a.id < b.id ? -1 : a.id > b.id ? 1 : 0),
+    );
+}
+
+/** The position for a new view: after the last one. */
+export function nextViewOrder(views: readonly SavedView[]): number {
+  return views.filter(isActive).reduce((max, view) => Math.max(max, view.order + 1), 0);
+}
+
+export type ViewNameProblem = 'empty' | 'duplicate';
+
+function nameKey(name: string): string {
+  return name.trim().toLocaleLowerCase();
+}
+
+/**
+ * Why a name can not be used, or null when it can. A name has to have something in it and can not
+ * repeat the name of another view (ignoring case and the spaces around it). Pass `ignoreId` when
+ * renaming, so a view does not clash with itself.
+ */
+export function viewNameProblem(
+  name: string,
+  views: readonly SavedView[],
+  ignoreId?: Id,
+): ViewNameProblem | null {
+  const key = nameKey(name);
+  if (key === '') return 'empty';
+  const taken = views.some(
+    (view) => isActive(view) && view.id !== ignoreId && nameKey(view.name) === key,
+  );
+  return taken ? 'duplicate' : null;
+}

+/** Lower case, without accents, with single spaces: "Ação  Rápida" and "acao rapida" are equal. */
+export function normalizeText(text: string): string {
+  return text.normalize('NFD').replace(/[̀-ͯ]/g, '').toLowerCase().replace(/\s+/g, ' ').trim();
+}
+
+/** The words of a search text, normalized. An empty or blank text has no words. */
+export function searchWords(text: string): string[] {
+  const normalized = normalizeText(text);
+  return normalized === '' ? [] : normalized.split(' ');
+}
+
+/** True when every word is somewhere in the haystack (already normalized by the caller or not). */
+export function containsAllWords(haystack: string, words: readonly string[]): boolean {
+  const target = normalizeText(haystack);
+  return words.every((word) => target.includes(word));
+}

+import type { DayPeriod, Id, ItemKind } from '../core';
+
+/**
+ * A chip of the "when" filter: one of the four day periods, or `untimed`, which stands for what has
+ * no set time of day: whole-day events and the task strips (open and overdue). A task due at 18:00
+ * is still untimed, because the hour is a limit, not time the person has booked.
+ */
+export type PeriodFilter = DayPeriod | 'untimed';
+
+/*
+ * What the person asked to see. Analogy: a set of sieves over the same pile of cards. Each sieve
+ * that is on keeps only some cards, and a card has to pass every sieve that is on. A sieve that is
+ * off (an empty list, an empty text, null) lets everything through.
+ *
+ * It is plain data (no functions, no dates), so a saved view can store it as JSON later.
+ */
+export interface ItemFilter {
+  /** Tags to show. A card passes with any of them, or any of their descendants. Empty means all. */
+  tagIds: Id[];
+  /** Kinds to show. A work block is an event. Empty means both. */
+  kinds: ItemKind[];
+  /**
+   * Chips of the "when" filter, "any of these". A day period keeps the timed events that touch it.
+   * `untimed` keeps whole-day events and the task strips. Only what is not covered by a chosen chip
+   * leaves, so "morning" alone shows just the morning events and "morning" plus "untimed" adds the
+   * whole-day events and the tasks. Empty means all.
+   */
+  periods: PeriodFilter[];
+  /** Words to find in the title, notes or location, all of them, ignoring case and accents. */
+  text: string;
+  /**
+   * Open tasks only show on a day when their delivery is at most this many days away from that
+   * day (0 means only on the delivery day). Overdue tasks always show. Null means no limit.
+   */
+  dueWithinDays: number | null;
+}
+
+export const EMPTY_FILTER: ItemFilter = {
+  tagIds: [],
+  kinds: [],
+  periods: [],
+  text: '',
+  dueWithinDays: null,
+};
+
+/** True when at least one sieve is on, so the interface can say that something is filtered. */
+export function isFilterActive(filter: ItemFilter): boolean {
+  return (
+    filter.tagIds.length > 0 ||
+    filter.kinds.length > 0 ||
+    filter.periods.length > 0 ||
+    filter.text.trim() !== '' ||
+    isValidDueWithin(filter.dueWithinDays)
+  );
+}
+
+/** A usable "due within" limit: a whole number of days, zero or more. Anything else is off. */
+export function isValidDueWithin(value: number | null): value is number {
+  return value !== null && Number.isInteger(value) && value >= 0;
+}

+import type { Table } from 'dexie';
+import { type SyncFields, type Timestamp } from '../core';
+import { ENTITY_KINDS, type AgendaDatabase, type EntityKind } from './db';
+import {
+  BACKUP_FORMAT,
+  BACKUP_VERSION,
+  findDanglingReferences,
+  parseBackup,
+  type BackupData,
+  type BackupFile,
+  type ImportIssue,
+} from './parseBackup';
+import { SEEDED_KEY } from './seed';
+import { SETTINGS_KEY, loadSettings } from './settings';
+
+export * from './parseBackup';
+
+export interface ExportOptions {
+  /** Keep deleted entities (tombstones) so that a later import can tell they were deleted. */
+  includeDeleted?: boolean;
+  now?: () => Timestamp;
+}
+
+/** Reads everything in one consistent snapshot. */
+export async function exportBackup(
+  db: AgendaDatabase,
+  options: ExportOptions = {},
+): Promise<BackupFile> {
+  const includeDeleted = options.includeDeleted ?? true;
+  const now = options.now ?? (() => new Date().toISOString());
+
+  return db.transaction(
+    'r',
+    [
+      db.agendas,
+      db.agendaGroups,
+      db.items,
+      db.tags,
+      db.statusGroups,
+      db.statuses,
+      db.savedViews,
+      db.meta,
+    ],
+    async () => {
+      const keep = <T extends SyncFields>(list: T[]) =>
+        includeDeleted ? list : list.filter((entity) => entity.deletedAt === null);
+      const data: BackupData = {
+        agendas: keep(await db.agendas.toArray()),
+        agendaGroups: keep(await db.agendaGroups.toArray()),
+        items: keep(await db.items.toArray()),
+        tags: keep(await db.tags.toArray()),
+        statusGroups: keep(await db.statusGroups.toArray()),
+        statuses: keep(await db.statuses.toArray()),
+        savedViews: keep(await db.savedViews.toArray()),
+      };
+      const hasSettings = (await db.meta.get(SETTINGS_KEY)) !== undefined;
+      return {
+        format: BACKUP_FORMAT,
+        version: BACKUP_VERSION,
+        exportedAt: now(),
+        settings: hasSettings ? await loadSettings(db) : null,
+        data,
+      };
+    },
+  );
+}
+
+export function serializeBackup(backup: BackupFile): string {
+  return JSON.stringify(backup, null, 2);
+}
+
+/** A suggested file name such as unified-agenda-2026-11-07.json. */
+export function backupFileName(exportedAt: Timestamp): string {
+  return `unified-agenda-${exportedAt.slice(0, 10)}.json`;
+}
+
+/**
+ * - merge: adds what is new and, for an id that exists on both sides, keeps the version with the
+ *   newest `updatedAt` (last write wins, a tie keeps the local one). Nothing is ever removed.
+ *   Settings are taken from the file only when this device has none saved.
+ * - replace: the device ends up equal to the file. Everything else is erased first.
+ */
+export type ImportMode = 'merge' | 'replace';
+
+export interface KindSummary {
+  added: number;
+  updated: number;
+  skipped: number;
+}
+
+export type ImportSummary = Record<EntityKind, KindSummary> & { settingsApplied: boolean };
+
+export type ImportResult =
+  { ok: true; summary: ImportSummary } | { ok: false; issues: ImportIssue[] };
+
+type AnyTable = Table<SyncFields, string>;
+
+async function mergeKind(table: AnyTable, incoming: readonly SyncFields[]): Promise<KindSummary> {
+  const current = await table.bulkGet(incoming.map((entity) => entity.id));
+  const toWrite: SyncFields[] = [];
+  const summary: KindSummary = { added: 0, updated: 0, skipped: 0 };
+  incoming.forEach((entity, index) => {
+    const existing = current[index];
+    if (!existing) {
+      summary.added++;
+      toWrite.push(entity);
+    } else if (Date.parse(entity.updatedAt) > Date.parse(existing.updatedAt)) {
+      summary.updated++;
+      toWrite.push(entity);
+    } else {
+      summary.skipped++;
+    }
+  });
+  await table.bulkPut(toWrite);
+  return summary;
+}
+
+/**
+ * Writes a parsed backup. It all happens in one transaction: if anything fails, nothing is
+ * changed. In replace mode the file must be able to stand alone, so references to things that are
+ * not in it are refused.
+ */
+export async function importBackup(
+  db: AgendaDatabase,
+  backup: BackupFile,
+  mode: ImportMode = 'merge',
+): Promise<ImportResult> {
+  if (mode === 'replace') {
+    const issues = findDanglingReferences(backup.data);
+    if (issues.length > 0) return { ok: false, issues };
+  }
+
+  const tables = [
+    db.agendas,
+    db.agendaGroups,
+    db.items,
+    db.tags,
+    db.statusGroups,
+    db.statuses,
+    db.savedViews,
+    db.meta,
+  ];
+  const summary = await db.transaction('rw', tables, async () => {
+    const result = {} as ImportSummary;
+    for (const kind of ENTITY_KINDS) {
+      const table = db.table(kind) as unknown as AnyTable;
+      const incoming: readonly SyncFields[] = backup.data[kind];
+      if (mode === 'replace') {
+        await table.clear();
+        await table.bulkPut([...incoming]);
+        result[kind] = { added: incoming.length, updated: 0, skipped: 0 };
+      } else {
+        result[kind] = await mergeKind(table, incoming);
+      }
+    }
+
+    let settingsApplied = false;
+    if (mode === 'replace') {
+      if (backup.settings) {
+        await db.meta.put({ key: SETTINGS_KEY, value: backup.settings });
+        settingsApplied = true;
+      } else {
+        await db.meta.delete(SETTINGS_KEY);
+      }
+    } else if (backup.settings && (await db.meta.get(SETTINGS_KEY)) === undefined) {
+      await db.meta.put({ key: SETTINGS_KEY, value: backup.settings });
+      settingsApplied = true;
+    }
+    // Imported data brings its own status groups, so the defaults must not be created later
+    await db.meta.put({ key: SEEDED_KEY, value: true });
+
+    result.settingsApplied = settingsApplied;
+    return result;
+  });
+  return { ok: true, summary };
+}
+
+/** Reads a backup file's text and imports it. */
+export async function importBackupText(
+  db: AgendaDatabase,
+  text: string,
+  mode: ImportMode = 'merge',
+): Promise<ImportResult> {
+  const parsed = parseBackup(text);
+  if (!parsed.ok) return { ok: false, issues: parsed.issues };
+  return importBackup(db, parsed.backup, mode);
+}

+import {
+  defaultContext,
+  descendantIds,
+  isActive,
+  softDelete,
+  tagWithDescendantIds,
+  updateEntity,
+  type Context,
+  type Id,
+  type Item,
+  type Tag,
+} from '../core';
+import type { AgendaDatabase } from './db';
+
+/*
+ * Deleting an agenda or an item also deletes what lives inside it. Everything is only marked
+ * with `deletedAt` (a tombstone), in one transaction, so a failure never leaves half a tree.
+ */
+
+export interface RemovalResult {
+  /** False when the id does not exist or was already deleted. Nothing changed then. */
+  removed: boolean;
+  /** How many items were marked as deleted, the item itself included. */
+  items: number;
+}
+
+const NOTHING: RemovalResult = { removed: false, items: 0 };
+
+async function activeItems(db: AgendaDatabase): Promise<Item[]> {
+  return (await db.items.toArray()).filter(isActive);
+}
+
+/** The given roots plus everything below them, at any depth. */
+function withDescendants(rootIds: Iterable<Id>, items: readonly Item[]): Set<Id> {
+  const ids = new Set<Id>();
+  for (const root of rootIds) {
+    ids.add(root);
+    for (const id of descendantIds(root, items)) ids.add(id);
+  }
+  return ids;
+}
+
+function agendaItemIds(agendaId: Id, items: readonly Item[]): Set<Id> {
+  const roots = items.filter((item) => item.agendaId === agendaId).map((item) => item.id);
+  return withDescendants(roots, items);
+}
+
+function subtreeIds(itemId: Id, items: readonly Item[]): Set<Id> {
+  return items.some((item) => item.id === itemId) ? withDescendants([itemId], items) : new Set();
+}
+
+/** How many items deleting this agenda would delete. For the confirmation message. */
+export async function countAgendaItems(db: AgendaDatabase, agendaId: Id): Promise<number> {
+  return agendaItemIds(agendaId, await activeItems(db)).size;
+}
+
+/** How many items deleting this item would delete, itself included. */
+export async function countItemSubtree(db: AgendaDatabase, itemId: Id): Promise<number> {
+  return subtreeIds(itemId, await activeItems(db)).size;
+}
+
+/** Deletes an item and all its sub-items and work blocks. */
+export function removeItemCascade(
+  db: AgendaDatabase,
+  itemId: Id,
+  ctx: Context = defaultContext,
+): Promise<RemovalResult> {
+  return db.transaction('rw', db.items, async () => {
+    const items = await activeItems(db);
+    const ids = subtreeIds(itemId, items);
+    if (ids.size === 0) return NOTHING;
+    await db.items.bulkPut(items.filter((item) => ids.has(item.id)).map((i) => softDelete(i, ctx)));
+    return { removed: true, items: ids.size };
+  });
+}
+
+/**
+ * Deletes an agenda, every item in it, and takes it out of the agenda groups and the saved views
+ * that list it. A view that listed only this agenda goes back to showing every agenda, which is
+ * what the selection already did when all its agendas were gone.
+ */
+export function removeAgendaCascade(
+  db: AgendaDatabase,
+  agendaId: Id,
+  ctx: Context = defaultContext,
+): Promise<RemovalResult> {
+  return db.transaction('rw', db.agendas, db.agendaGroups, db.items, db.savedViews, async () => {
+    const agenda = await db.agendas.get(agendaId);
+    if (!agenda || !isActive(agenda)) return NOTHING;
+
+    const items = await activeItems(db);
+    const ids = agendaItemIds(agendaId, items);
+    await db.items.bulkPut(items.filter((item) => ids.has(item.id)).map((i) => softDelete(i, ctx)));
+
+    const groups = (await db.agendaGroups.toArray()).filter(
+      (group) => isActive(group) && group.agendaIds.includes(agendaId),
+    );
+    await db.agendaGroups.bulkPut(
+      groups.map((group) =>
+        updateEntity(group, { agendaIds: group.agendaIds.filter((id) => id !== agendaId) }, ctx),
+      ),
+    );
+
+    const views = (await db.savedViews.toArray()).filter(
+      (view) => isActive(view) && view.agendaIds?.includes(agendaId),
+    );
+    await db.savedViews.bulkPut(
+      views.map((view) => {
+        const left = view.agendaIds!.filter((id) => id !== agendaId);
+        return updateEntity(view, { agendaIds: left.length > 0 ? left : null }, ctx);
+      }),
+    );
+
+    await db.agendas.put(softDelete(agenda, ctx));
+    return { removed: true, items: ids.size };
+  });
+}
+
+export interface TagUsage {
+  /** Sub-tags (at any depth) that would be deleted with the tag. The tag itself is not counted. */
+  subTags: number;
+  /** Active items that carry the tag or any of its sub-tags. */
+  items: number;
+}
+
+async function activeTags(db: AgendaDatabase): Promise<Tag[]> {
+  return (await db.tags.toArray()).filter(isActive);
+}
+
+/** What deleting this tag would touch. For the confirmation message. */
+export async function countTagUsage(db: AgendaDatabase, tagId: Id): Promise<TagUsage> {
+  const tags = await activeTags(db);
+  if (!tags.some((tag) => tag.id === tagId)) return { subTags: 0, items: 0 };
+  const ids = tagWithDescendantIds(tagId, tags);
+  const items = (await activeItems(db)).filter((item) => item.tagIds.some((id) => ids.has(id)));
+  return { subTags: ids.size - 1, items: items.length };
+}
+
+/**
+ * Deletes a tag and its sub-tags, and takes them off every item and saved view that carried them.
+ * The items and views stay. Only the ones that changed get a new `updatedAt`. All in one
+ * transaction.
+ */
+export function removeTagCascade(
+  db: AgendaDatabase,
+  tagId: Id,
+  ctx: Context = defaultContext,
+): Promise<{ removed: boolean; subTags: number; items: number }> {
+  return db.transaction('rw', db.tags, db.items, db.savedViews, async () => {
+    const tags = await activeTags(db);
+    if (!tags.some((tag) => tag.id === tagId)) return { removed: false, subTags: 0, items: 0 };
+
+    const ids = tagWithDescendantIds(tagId, tags);
+    await db.tags.bulkPut(tags.filter((tag) => ids.has(tag.id)).map((tag) => softDelete(tag, ctx)));
+
+    const touched = (await activeItems(db)).filter((item) => item.tagIds.some((id) => ids.has(id)));
+    await db.items.bulkPut(
+      touched.map((item) =>
+        updateEntity(item, { tagIds: item.tagIds.filter((id) => !ids.has(id)) }, ctx),
+      ),
+    );
+
+    const views = (await db.savedViews.toArray()).filter(
+      (view) => isActive(view) && view.filter.tagIds.some((id) => ids.has(id)),
+    );
+    await db.savedViews.bulkPut(
+      views.map((view) =>
+        updateEntity(
+          view,
+          { filter: { ...view.filter, tagIds: view.filter.tagIds.filter((id) => !ids.has(id)) } },
+          ctx,
+        ),
+      ),
+    );
+    return { removed: true, subTags: ids.size - 1, items: touched.length };
+  });
+}

+import Dexie, { type EntityTable } from 'dexie';
+import type { Agenda, AgendaGroup, Item, SavedView, Status, StatusGroup, Tag } from '../core';
+
+/*
+ * The local database, kept in IndexedDB (the browser's built-in database) through Dexie.
+ *
+ * Schema rules:
+ * - Never edit a version that has shipped. A change adds `db.version(n + 1)` with `.stores()`
+ *   for the new indexes and an `.upgrade()` step that moves the old data.
+ * - Only fields used in a query are indexed. Everything else is stored but not searched here:
+ *   the views filter in memory with the pure functions of the core.
+ * - A key that is empty (`null`) cannot be indexed in IndexedDB, so `deletedAt` is listed for
+ *   completeness and the code filters on it in memory.
+ */
+
+export const DEFAULT_DB_NAME = 'unified-agenda';
+
+/** One row of small app data, such as the settings or the "defaults were created" mark. */
+export interface MetaRecord {
+  key: string;
+  value: unknown;
+}
+
+export type AgendaDatabase = Dexie & {
+  agendas: EntityTable<Agenda, 'id'>;
+  agendaGroups: EntityTable<AgendaGroup, 'id'>;
+  items: EntityTable<Item, 'id'>;
+  tags: EntityTable<Tag, 'id'>;
+  savedViews: EntityTable<SavedView, 'id'>;
+  statusGroups: EntityTable<StatusGroup, 'id'>;
+  statuses: EntityTable<Status, 'id'>;
+  meta: EntityTable<MetaRecord, 'key'>;
+};
+
+/** The tables that hold entities, in the order the backup file lists them. */
+export const ENTITY_KINDS = [
+  'agendas',
+  'agendaGroups',
+  'items',
+  'tags',
+  'statusGroups',
+  'statuses',
+  'savedViews',
+] as const;
+
+export type EntityKind = (typeof ENTITY_KINDS)[number];
+
+export function createDatabase(name: string = DEFAULT_DB_NAME): AgendaDatabase {
+  const db = new Dexie(name) as AgendaDatabase;
+  db.version(1).stores({
+    agendas: 'id, order, updatedAt, deletedAt',
+    agendaGroups: 'id, order, updatedAt, deletedAt',
+    items: 'id, parentId, agendaId, statusId, *tagIds, updatedAt, deletedAt',
+    tags: 'id, parentId, updatedAt, deletedAt',
+    statusGroups: 'id, order, updatedAt, deletedAt',
+    statuses: 'id, groupId, order, updatedAt, deletedAt',
+    meta: 'key',
+  });
+  // Version 2 adds the saved views. A new table needs no `upgrade` step: nothing has to move.
+  db.version(2).stores({
+    savedViews: 'id, order, updatedAt, deletedAt',
+  });
+  return db;
+}
